description: A two-panel composite figure of optical micrographs of fully austenitic lightweight steels, both etched in 10% nital. (a) is a bright-field optical micrograph with a black 100 µm scale bar at lower right, showing coarse primary austenite dendrites: tan-to-orange dendrite arms with secondary arms arranged in a cross/dendritic pattern, separated by darker bluish-grey interdendritic regions, with small dark spherical inclusions scattered throughout. (b) is a differential interference contrast (DIC) optical micrograph with a black 50 µm scale bar at lower right, showing a much finer, fully recrystallised structure: equiaxed austenite grains rendered in various interference colours (purple, orange, brown, tan) that contain parallel-line annealing twins, with bright white second-phase particles decorating many grain boundaries and also sitting inside grains. The caption identifies (a) as as-cast Fe-28Mn-3Al-0.9Si-1.2C-0.6Mo steel and (b) as hot-rolled Fe-29Mn-6Al-0.9C-0.29Si-0.44Nb-0.44Mo steel, and states the average grain size in (b) is 50 µm. Together the panels demonstrate that hot rolling converts millimetre-scale as-cast dendrites into fine equiaxed austenite grains with annealing twins, pinned by NbC at grain boundaries.

subfigures.description: Bright-field optical micrograph with a 100 µm scale bar (lower right) of as-cast steel: coarse primary austenite dendrites with secondary arms forming a cross/dendritic pattern, orange-tan dendrite cores against darker bluish-grey interdendritic regions, plus small dark spherical inclusions. No numeric axis labels.

Differential interference contrast (DIC) optical micrograph with a 50 µm scale bar (lower right) of hot-rolled steel: fine equiaxed austenite grains in varied interference colours (purple, orange, brown, tan), numerous parallel-line annealing twins within grains, and bright white particles (stated to be NbC) at grain boundaries and in grain interiors.

observations.observation: Panel (a) carries a black scale bar labelled 100 µm in the lower-right corner.
Panel (a) shows a coarse dendritic morphology: lighter orange-tan dendrite arms with secondary arms in a cross-like pattern enclosed by darker bluish-grey interdendritic regions.
Panel (a) contains small dark spherical inclusions distributed across both dendrite cores and interdendritic regions.
Panel (b) carries a black scale bar labelled 50 µm in the lower-right corner, i.e. half the magnification scale of panel (a).
Panel (b) shows equiaxed grains of many different interference colours (purple, orange, brown, tan) containing sets of parallel straight striations identified as annealing twins.
Panel (b) contains numerous bright white particulate features located both on grain boundaries and inside grains.
The caption states that (a) is a bright-field optical micrograph of an as-cast Fe-28Mn-3Al-0.9Si-1.2C-0.6Mo steel with a microstructure of large primary austenite dendrites.
The caption states that (b) is a hot-rolled Fe-29Mn-6Al-0.9C-0.29Si-0.44Nb-0.44Mo steel consisting of equiaxed austenite grains and annealing twins with an average grain size of 50 µm.
The caption states that the white particles in (b) are NbC pinning the grain boundaries.
The caption states that (b) was imaged using differential interference contrast imaging and that both specimens were etched using 10% nital.
The citing text states that as-cast alloys consist of large primary austenitic dendrites that produce grain structures on the order of millimeters.
The citing text states that hot rolling refines the grain size and that the steel in Fig. 1b consists of fine equiaxed austenite grains and annealing twins.
